title: Six Canadian Banks Explore Tokenized CAD Deposits
summary:
Key Takeaways: Six major Canadian banks are collaborating on Canadian dollar tokenized deposits to enable centralized, programmable, and fast digital payments. The first stage will involve the transfer of tokenized
The post Six Canadian Banks Explore Tokenized CAD Deposits appeared first on CryptoNi...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Six major Canadian banks are collaborating on Canadian dollar tokenized deposits to enable centralized, programmable, and fast digital payments.
  • The first stage will involve the transfer of tokenized deposits among financial institutions in Canada.
  • As Canada develops its crypto framework, the project can be scaled up later to connect bank-based digital money with other digital asset projects.

Canada’s financial industry is making an even bigger leap into blockchain money. Six of the nation’s largest banks are collaborating on a tokenized deposit program aimed at bringing modernization to the movement of Canadian-dollar deposits through the financial system.

  • Six Banks Join the Tokenized Deposit Project
  • Tokenized Deposits vs. Stablecoins
    • Canada Expands Its Digital Asset Rules

Six Banks Join the Tokenized Deposit Project

The initiative includes Bank of Montreal, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, National Bank of Canada, Royal Bank of Canada, Scotiabank and TD Bank Group. The banks indicated that the project will be used to help the development of digital money, with a focus on remaining secure and stable, as well as being regulated.

The project is different from creating a new cryptocurrency; it is about tokenizing deposits in regulated banks. At present, the first phase is likely to discuss transferring these digital deposits seamlessly between the participating financial institutions.

The banks also announced they believe other deposit-taking institutions may be interested in that eventually as well.

Read More: Ondo Unlocks $3.6B Tokenized Market With Direct Stock-to-Token Conversions

Tokenized Deposits vs. Stablecoins

From a crypto market point of view, tokenized deposits and stablecoins can resemble their counterpart financial products, but they are not identical assets.

OSFI clarified on Sept. 10 that tokenized deposits are not legally distinct from traditional deposits simply because blockchain or other technology is used. A technology neutral approach is taken by the regulator, in that they do not judge the legal characteristics of the financial product depending on the underlying technology.

That matters because banks are increasingly branching out into the digital asset space. A tokenized deposit can be linked to the underlying bank deposit, whereas a fiat-backed stablecoin is a new digital currency that is issued under its respective regulatory system.

Read More: SEC Eyes Tokenized Stocks Plan That Could Unlock Trillions in Crypto Trading Markets

Canada Expands Its Digital Asset Rules

The banking system initiative comes at a time when Canada is developing a wider plan for the digital money infrastructure. The Stablecoin Act was part of Bill C-15 that was proclaimed in March 2026, establishing a federal framework for issuing cryptocurrencies monetized by a stable tie to fiat currency.

According to the architecture, anyone assembling non-financial institution stablecoins will have to register with the Bank of Canada, maintain reserves at the Bank’s cost, and redeem stablecoins at par. The framework is being drafted and will be implemented by 2027.

The six-bank project thus brings another layer to Canada’s digital payment ecosystem, as banks try to understand how tokenized deposits can be regulated, and the regulator and other policy makers continue to develop rules for stablecoins and other digital payment technologies.

title: Coinbase Tracks $1.1M Crypto Trail as Microsoft Takes Down 175 EvilTokens Domains
summary:
Key Takeaways: Between October 2025 and June 2026, approximately $1.1 million was traced from several Tron addresses belonging to Coinbase for these crypto assets associated with EvilTokens. Over 1,000 deposits
The post Coinbase Tracks $1.1M Crypto Trail as Microsoft Takes Down 175 EvilTokens Domain...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Between October 2025 and June 2026, approximately $1.1 million was traced from several Tron addresses belonging to Coinbase for these crypto assets associated with EvilTokens.
  • Over 1,000 deposits from over 700 crypto addresses were detected in the platform’s payment stream.
  • Microsoft and its partners seized 50 websites and disabled over 175 domains associated with the AI-based phishing attack.

Coinbase has joined Microsoft and several security organizations in disrupting EvilTokens, a phishing-as-a-service platform that uses AI to help criminals compromise email accounts and redirect financial payments, including cryptocurrency. The crypto exchange’s role focused on tracing the money behind the operation and identifying users connected to the service.

We partnered with Microsoft to disrupt EvilTokens, an AI-powered cybercrime platform.

Our team joined a global effort to dismantle its operations – investigating infrastructure, taking down domains, and helping police arrest its operators.

Say goodbye to another major… pic.twitter.com/myu0II6EwX

— Coinbase 🛡️ (@coinbase) September 22, 2026

  • Coinbase Follows EvilTokens’ Crypto Money Trail
  • Crypto Payments Became an Investigative Trail
    • AI Turned Phishing Into a Crypto Fraud Pipeline
    • 175+ Domains Disrupted

Coinbase Follows EvilTokens’ Crypto Money Trail

EvilTokens is a pre-packaged cybercrime service that is issued via Telegram. Criminal customers can use its tools to launch phishing, steal email access and research an infected mailbox for targeted information.

Payment infrastructure was a key link for Coinbase to crypto. EvilTokens accepted cryptocurrency as a service and would eventually make its money through the addresses of the TRON blockchain.

From Oct. 2025 and up to June 2026, the Global Intelligence team at Coinbase identified some $1.1 million in transactions that generated revenue on Coinbase’s messaging systems; that includes on the platform’s application. Investigators were able to trace over 1,000 deposits from well over 700 different addresses and track the money from there.

Read More: Coinbase Opens $2.2B IPO Door to US Retail Traders in Crypto Exchange Expansion

Crypto Payments Became an Investigative Trail

The case illustrates a common theme in crypto-related cybercrime investigations: blockchain transactions can offer investigators a trail of payments even when the perpetrators try using several wallets.

It added that it also looked at the customers of EvilTokens who are identified on its platform and notified law enforcement accordingly. The company said its records and membership had not been infiltrated during the campaign.

Others, however, were duped by cracking into their Coinbase accounts and tricked into transferring their cryptocurrencies straight to scam addresses.

AI Turned Phishing Into a Crypto Fraud Pipeline

A mix of account takeovers and AI-driven analysis was seen in EvilTokens. After gaining access to an inbox, its tools could determine trusted relationships, find payment-related conversations and uncover who is best to be impersonated.

There were over 12,000 compromised inboxes across over 10,000 organizations connected to the platform, Microsoft reported. It struck industries ranging from financial services to healthcare, construction, real estate and higher education.

It also masqueraded with Microsoft’s device-code authentication procedure. In this way, victims were directed to fake login pages, and codes were entered into Microsoft’s legitimate login page, allowing the attacker to login without stealing the victims’ password.

175+ Domains Disrupted

Microsoft and Health-ISAC pursued legal action in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, while Coinbase, Cloudflare, OpenAI, Railway, SpyCloud, TRM Labs and The Shadowserver Foundation contributed to the wider disruption effort.

During the operation, it was the seizure of 50 websites as well as blocking of over 175 domains in EvilTokens infrastructure. UK police also arrested two men on September 11 as part of the investigation, according to Microsoft and Coinbase.

For the crypto sector, the operation shows how on-chain financial intelligence can complement conventional cybersecurity investigations when cryptocurrency is used to monetize phishing and business-email fraud.

title: Pi Network Targets 914K Users With Major KYC and Mainnet Migration Fixes
summary:
Key Takeaways: Pi has now addressed an issue with duplicate-account verification, paving the way for over 417,000 Pioneers to continue with the KYC. A planned fix will aim to free
The post Pi Network Targets 914K Users With Major KYC and Mainnet Migration Fixes appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Pi has now addressed an issue with duplicate-account verification, paving the way for over 417,000 Pioneers to continue with the KYC.
  • A planned fix will aim to free up another 497,000 users who could not claim their migrated PI due to gas-fee problems from their Fast-Track wallets.
  • Pi also expanded liveness-check support, launched a trial for palm-print authentication, and implemented new KYC resubmission options.

Pi Network is implementing a set of technical updates in response to the KYC and Mainnet migration issues impeding users. The total number of Pioneers impacted by the updates is approximately 914,000, but there are some technical challenges faced by each group and all must satisfy applicable requirements.

Pi has released several technical updates to KYC and Mainnet migration processes that address specific KYC application corner cases, improve verification processes, and help eligible Pioneers who were previously unable to progress.

KYC and Mainnet migration involve many…

— Pi Network (@PiCoreTeam) September 22, 2026

  • 417,000 Pioneers Clear a KYC Roadblock
  • Fast-Track Wallets Face a Separate Gas Problem
    • Pi Expands KYC Verification Options

417,000 Pioneers Clear a KYC Roadblock

Pi has improved the reviewing process of those accounts that have been previously flagged as potential duplicate accounts. Following further testing, over 417,000 Pioneer accounts were marked as non-duplications allowing for further progress to be made in KYC.

The change doesn’t necessarily represent the completion of KYC. They need to continue to fulfill the remaining identity checks and other requirements to be able to migrate to the Mainnet.

Pi commented that these cases may present individual technical challenges as various groups may freeze for various reasons. After a given issue is reviewed, tested and fixed, the users with that issue(s) will be released in bits and pieces.

Fast-Track Wallets Face a Separate Gas Problem

A Mainnet migration problem affecting Fast-Track wallets impacts another 497,000 Pioneers.

These wallets have gone through a different KYC path and were subsequently destination wallets following a Mainnet migration. Some users were not able to retrieve their migrated balances due to insufficient balance in their wallets to pay for gas fees, Pi said.

Pi said that within the next week, the update was going to be released to resolve the problem before it can happen again in future migrations.

Read More: Binance Wallet Opens $4.7T Pre-IPO Market Access Through PancakeSwap Tokenized Deals

Pi Expands KYC Verification Options

The latest addition also addresses a number of minor KYC hurdles. Pi has optimised its technical workflows in order to minimise the occurrence of errors linked to processing intensively used video-based and automated KYC checks. It has also allowed for earlier applicants in the Yoti KYC process to re-apply for service when required liveness data was missing.

Livemodes eligibility may also be extended for older or lower specification phones. Pi additionally enhanced how its system captures face angle to enable a higher number of devices to finish the verification procedure.

For selected Pioneers, Pi has started a one-month palm-print authentication trial. As users undergo repeated liveness checks, the test is intended to offer a further means of authentication without requiring the face to be displayed during the specific liveness check step.

In addition, Pi has added a new resubmission channel for impacted users in Indonesia whose KIA identification documents were previously not acceptable for KYC purposes.

title: ECB Launches Pontes to Move €1.6B Tokenized Market Into Central Bank Money
summary:
Key Takeaways: The European Central Bank has launched Pontes, a tool that will allow wholesale transactions of tokens to be settled using the bank’s money. The ECB states that the
The post ECB Launches Pontes to Move €1.6B Tokenized Market Into Central Bank Money appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The European Central Bank has launched Pontes, a tool that will allow wholesale transactions of tokens to be settled using the bank’s money.
  • The ECB states that the system underwent the Eurosystem tests with approximately €1.6 billion over 50 tests in 2024.
  • Pontes will gradually increase its features and hours of operation, and complete implementation will be sought for by 2028.

The European Central Bank is now directly backing the infrastructure behind tokenized European financial markets with central bank money. The launch of Pontes gives banks and market infrastructures a new route to settle blockchain-based wholesale transactions using a central-bank settlement asset.

  • Pontes Connects Tokenized Markets to Central Bank Money
  • Banks and DLT Operators Join the Initial Rollout
    • Pontes Expands Through 2028

Pontes Connects Tokenized Markets to Central Bank Money

Pontes aims to connect market-based distributed ledger technologies (DLT) platforms with Eurosystem’s existing services TARGET Services. It has a first use to effect settlement of wholesale trades in tokenized assets, without releasing the cash leg into central bank money.

This action comes to light as an important challenge for tokenized finance, especially regarding the full settlement of digital securities without the use of private settlement assets.

The process of tokenization is that of creating a digital representation (token) of financial or real-world assets on DLT networks. It can help to align issuance and trading, settlement and various aspects of the transaction lifecycle, with the help of smart contracts being used at wholesale markets.

Pontes’ exploratory work 2024 contributed to the ECB. In the 50 trials by the Eurosystem in nine jurisdictions, worth of transactions run around €1.6 billion, and participants stated that having easy access to a risk-free finding of the settlement asset is vital for general adoption of DLT-based markets.

Read More: SEC Clears Path for Tokenized Stocks With 5-Year Onchain Trading Exemption

Banks and DLT Operators Join the Initial Rollout

Pontes is rolling out an incremental onboarding process and NOT making a mass consumer launch. An initial cohort of financial firms and DLT operators has already been completely onboarded and can use the system, the ECB said. 

It includes a range of banks, like Deutsche Bank, Santander and Société Générale, and market infrastructures like Clearstream and SWIAT. More people are anticipated to join in the next few months.

Pontes Expands Through 2028

As a core basis, the first version of Pontes offers services along with some extra capabilities, which will be expanded over time. The ECB aims to have the system in full use by 2028.

Pontes has a broader Eurosystem plan for tokenized finance too. The complementary Appia initiative is currently going on the longer-term design of an integrated DT-based European financial services ecosystem, with an envisioned blueprint in 2028.

The ECB has also been working like crazy on preparations to hold a small amount of its own assets in such tokenized securities. It plans to complete those purchases using Pontes, which began with euro-denominated bonds issued by public-sector and European supranational entities.

The launch establishes the central bank’s settlement infrastructure at the heart of crypto and tokenized-asset markets, providing institutional participants with yet another infrastructure on which to rely to develop and settle digital asset transactions in Europe.
